headline: InfoPPO uses information-time discounting and adaptive clipping for long-horizon language-model RL
summary: A September 21, 2026 arXiv paper introduces InfoPPO, which measures temporal progression in RLVR by accumulated information density rather than raw token count and uses that density to adapt policy clipping. In author-reported Mean@16 results across five competition-style mathematics benchmarks, average accuracy for Qwen3-4B/8B/14B is 34.9/41.2/49.4, compared with DAPO at 32.2/36.3/45.3. The paper reports response lengths broadly comparable to DAPO/DAPO-FT and shorter than PPO in its table, and adds one Llama-3.2-3B appendix comparison. These are CLAIMED paper results, not independently reproduced; no seed-level uncertainty is reported in the main aggregate table, and task/model transfer remains open.
